title: coalition-watch-closure-notes-2027-02-14
body:
TL;DR:
Evening watch observed a short-lived cascade of 503s impacting hosted inference traffic to us-west-2 between 18:03–18:21 PST. Root cause appears to be repeated large prefix evictions in kv-cache-proxy triggered by a small set of high-token-length requests from an experimental customer (client X). We mitigated by temporarily disabling eviction aggressiveness and routing heavy tails to dedicated throughput lane (policy: route-to-dedicated). Error rate returned to baseline by 18:22. Post-mortem follow-ups and runbook edits below.

What I saw (observational notes):
- 18:01: steady traffic, 99th latency ~180ms, error rate ~0.02%.
- 18:03: spike in 5xxs from gateway; frontend-api returned 503s for ~3–8% of requests for 1 minute.
- 18:04–18:08: kv-cache-proxy reported repeated cache eviction churn (logs: repeated DeletePrefix for large prefix ranges).
- 18:05: request-router started queueing at the batching-service; some batches timed out at 10s.
- 18:08: applied temporary policy: reduce kv-cache eviction aggressiveness (parameter: max-prefix-evict-per-sec from 1000 -> 100), and enabled route-to-dedicated for flows with token_length > 5000.
- 18:12: queue depth fell, 5xxs dropped to baseline.
- 18:22: system stable, monitoring returned to normal.

Immediate mitigation actions performed (commands & notes):
- Riley: applied config to kv-cache-proxy via config-service: set max-prefix-evict-per-sec=100 (rollback plan documented).
- Miguel: updated routing policy in request-router to tag and divert large-token requests to dedicated pool (policy revision id: RR-2027-02-14-1).
- Samira: raised rate-limit for experimental customer X and throttled long-running streaming sessions.
- Asha: incremented alert threshold temporarily to avoid alert storms while we stabilized.

Suspected root cause and hypothesis:
- Root cause chain: a small fraction of extremely long-context requests (token_length > ~5k) caused disproportionate cache churn in kv-cache-proxy because eviction logic iterates prefixes in O(n) with large prefix ranges. The churn caused increased CPU on serving nodes and created transient timeouts in batching-service, leading to upstream 503s.
- Secondary factors: missing guardrail in request-router for token-length tagging, and eviction parameters tuned for steady-state but not spikey long-tail traffic.

Data and logs to review (next shift):
- kv-cache-proxy logs: grep for DeletePrefix and eviction-duration between 17:55–18:25 (Riley).
- request-router traces for diverted vs non-diverted flows (Miguel).
- Batching-service timeout histograms and logs for 10s timeouts (Samira).
- Customer X session logs to understand workload patterns and whether an automated job caused the spike (owner: account-ops).

Runbook deltas (suggested edits) — please review:
- Add a new section "Large-context workload protection": add token_length tagging at request-router level and automatic routing to dedicated or throttled lanes when token_length > 3k.
- Update kv-cache-proxy playbook to include a K-step for reducing eviction aggressiveness and a clear rollback command pair. Document the safe min and max for max-prefix-evict-per-sec.
- Add an observability dashboard: Kv-cache prefix eviction rate, eviction CPU, and correlated batch timeout rate for quick triage.
- Include a checklist for evening/midnight watch: confirm routing policy and eviction thresholds are present in config-service.

Follow-ups / action items (owner — due):
- Riley: Extract eviction traces and prepare a short diagnostic (logs + flamegraph) for the infra retrospective. Due 2027-02-17.
- Miguel: Implement token_length tagging PR in request-router and add unit/integration tests. Link PR to incident. Due 2027-02-21.
- Samira: Add batch-timeout SLO dashboard and set an alert that triggers before user-visible 5xx thresholds. Due 2027-02-18.
- Asha: Draft customer communication template for experimental customers with heavy tails; sync with account-ops. Due 2027-02-16.
- Eng-serve owner (TBD): Investigate algorithmic optimization for kv-cache eviction to avoid O(n) prefix scans for large ranges. Create RFC if needed. Due 2027-03-01.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Was the traffic from customer X human-driven or a job loop? Ask account-ops for session schedule.
- Do we want an automatic hard-limit for token_length at API gateway to protect hosted customers? Pros/cons doc required.
- Can batch timeouts be backoff-aware so large-context requests are processed separately without blocking short requests?

Communications / who informed:
- Pagerduty: incident created and assigned to SRE oncall at 18:05.
- Slack #sre-ops: brief posted 18:06 by Asha.
- Account-ops: PM pinged at 18:10 about customer X.

Monitoring notes (alerts & thresholds):
- Adjusted alert: kv-cache-eviction-rate-high (silenced during mitigation window 18:06–18:20).
- New proposed alert: batch-timeout-rate > 0.5% for 5m should trigger P2.
- Add metric: request_router.token_length.p50/p95/p99 to dashboard.

Post-incident retrospective plan:
- Schedule quick blameless 30-min sync Thu 2027-02-18 09:30 PST (owners: Riley, Miguel, Samira, Asha). Agenda: validate root cause, review runbook edits, confirm follow-ups.
- Week-after deep dive: eng-serve to propose eviction algorithm improvements.

Night watch checklist (prep for next shift):
- Verify RR-2027-02-14-1 is active and token_length tagging works (Miguel).
- Confirm kv-cache max-prefix-evict-per-sec remains at 100 and track eviction CPU. (Riley).
- Confirm account-ops reached out to customer X about anomalous usage. (Asha).

Misc notes / rough thinking (brainstorm):
- Consider adding a lightweight per-request token_budget that cancels prefix eviction for requests under N tokens.
- Explore incremental eviction (windowed eviction with rate limiting per prefix) to avoid bursts.
- Potential longer-term: per-customer cache partitions to isolate noisy tenants.

If anything regresses overnight, re-escalate immediately to oncall lead and follow the existing incident escalation matrix.

-- Asha (evening watch)
